newsitem.title: UK: Coffee, silver sink but base metals off 6-mth peaks.
newsitem.headline: Coffee, silver sink but base metals off 6-mth peaks.

text.p: Coffee prices sank to a 31-month-low on Thursday on widespread selling ahead of November's expiry while silver was fixed at a new 20-month-low following slumps in other precious metals.
Elsewhere, copper and aluminium backed down slightly after hitting six-month-peaks earlier in the day on persistent concern over low stocks and high backwardations.
Coffee futures, regaining volatility this week after a lull, hit the lowest levels since April 1994 on speculative and fund selling.
Benchmark January futures lost $38 to close at $1,342 a tonne after sellers knocked the prices down to below the key $1,360 support.
The spot November contract also fell sharply on long liquidation amid concerns of mounting nearby supplies. The contract expires on Friday.
Traders said coffee's sharp downward move was mainly technically driven amid a dearth of significant physical news.
Silver was fixed at 472.75 cents an ounce, its lowest fixing since March 28, 1995 in line with falling gold prices. Silver was fixed at 474 cents on Wednesday.
Gold has fallen over $10 per ounce in the past month as disillusioned speculators abandoned the metal and silver prices have dropped about 20 cents in the past five days.
Gold was fixed at $372.20 an ounce in the morning, the lowest setting since April 25, 1994.
Silver came under pressure after an attempt by speculators to take the price back over $5.00, where it hasn't been since mid October, failed last week.
In base metals, three-months delivery copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) found light support at $2,260 a tonne after coming off six-month highs above $2,300 earlier in the day.

Copper pulled back on market talk of an LME stock rise on Friday. Dealings were brisk despite U.S. Thanksgiving holiday. Aluminium also came off its high of $1,571 a tonne in the morning. But it met support around $1,550.
Many traders were wary of current advances in aluminium, which were largely motivated by speculators. Users are keeping to the sidelines, while producers might sell around $1,600.
Elsewhere, cocoa settled in the minus territory as the market consolidated from this week's recent gains.
U.S. commodities markets were closed for Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday and Friday.
The London markets are closed at 1700 GMT on Thursday and Friday.
